text: {"headline":"High 99215 share concentrated on low-complexity patients is consistent with upcoding, but the few returned charts support the billed levels, so documentation is too thin to confirm.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern leans toward concern. More than half of this provider's 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, and the 99215 share is several times the all-provider rate in every complexity stratum, including zero-condition visits. The sampled low-complexity 99215s carry routine diagnoses such as UTI (N39.0, e.g., C0017692, C0017700, C0017765), URI (J06.9, C0017515) and rash (R21, C0017618). The high-complexity examples (e.g., C0017571, C0018209) look like the expected use of the code. The charts do not back up the concern: all 5 documented 99215s, and every documented 99213 and 99214, supported the billed level, and only 1 data-reviewed note lacked a lab line. With records for under 3% of claims, that is too few to judge either way, and cloned or templated notes cannot be ruled out. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, especially the N39.0, J06.9 and R21 visits, and check whether MDM and time are truly patient-specific rather than templated."}
